entry.title: Measure a Free Model Route With a Golden Set, Not a Leaderboard
entry.summary: The first number I track when evaluating a free model route is not the public benchmark delta. It is the semantic failure count in a 100-case golden set. A public benchmark can be flat while your application's specific tool calls, JSON schemas, and failure states move. I start with a golden set: 100–300 request/response pairs captured from the current route. Each case stores the expected tool call and a small list of acceptable result patterns. The set must include ambiguous prompts, permission denials, empty-result cases, and at least one request that should deliberately fail. If a candidate cannot reproduce that failure, it is not a drop-in route. The evaluator is deliberately boring.
